problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨6{t}^{2},\,\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{t}⟩,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $r=⟨-1,\,2⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position of $P$ at time $t=1.$ Do not round the answers.

$r(1)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨6{t}^{2},\,\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{t}⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 6{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t,\,\int \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{t}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2{t}^{3}+{C}_{1},\,\sqrt{{t}^{3}}+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨-1,2⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨2(0)^{3}+{C}_{1},\,\sqrt{(0)^{3}}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨-1,2⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we must have ${C}_{1}=-1$ and ${C}_{2}=2.$ Therefore, the position vector at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2{t}^{3}-1,\,\sqrt{{t}^{3}}+2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the position vector at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨2(1)^{3}-1,\,\sqrt{(1)^{3}}+2⟩ \\  & =⟨2-1,\,1+2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
